claims.text: This is the same trip on every artifact the rider relies on: EV-TRIP-00535, EV-GPS-00535 and EV-FARE-00535 all carry trip_id TRP-00535 with the pickup recorded at 06:50-06:56 on 23 September 2026, so the same-trip limb of POL-RD-08 is satisfied, the rider's initial burden is properly engaged, and no identifier-mismatch escalation under POL-RD-10 is in play.

The distance measurement is taken from an unimpaired trace and carries no discount: EV-GPS-00535 has 100% coverage, 403 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so it meets none of the impairment limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07, no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises, and every artifact the rider relies on sits at weight 1.0, so nothing is down-weighted under POL-GEN-02.

Candour on the threshold, because overstating it would cost the claim: the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km at 20.35 km against the booked optimal of 20.1 km, so the measured excess is 0.25 km, or 1.24%, which fails both the 0.8 km and the 20% limbs of POL-RD-01, and the platform's own derived deviation status reads 'no deviation'. On this record no distance deviation is established, and the rider does not contend otherwise; the app's estimate of 44 minutes against a 67-minute trip is a delay the route-deviation policy does not price.

If the tribunal nevertheless finds the excess sufficient under POL-RD-01, the refund is arithmetic rather than discretionary and is the platform's own figure: against a charged total on EV-FARE-00535 of SGD 38.66, the recomputation yields SGD 32.32250 against the closure-adjusted optimal, a return of SGD 6.35, or SGD 6.70 against the unadjusted optimal. The rider's ask is confined to the lower figure, SGD 6.35, and not the SGD 30.00 first contested.

The SGD 30.00 the rider contested is the consequential cost of the missed connection, not a line of the metered fare, and POL-RD-02 prices only the distance and time lines of the fare_breakdown; the rider does not ask the tribunal to award a head of loss the policy does not provide, and confines its substantive ask to the fare recomputation, leaving the ruling vocabulary of POL-GEN-03 to do the rest.

claims.text: No route deviation is established under POL-RD-01. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km at 20.35 km against the booked optimal of 20.1 km, an excess of 0.25 km — 1.24% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, both tests passing; 0.25 km fails both, and the platform's own derived deviation status reads 'no deviation'. Where either establishment test fails the clause directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree the trace governs, and that the rounded trip-record figure may NOT be cited for the threshold test. Even on the rider's most favourable reading of trip_record.actual_distance_km at 20.4 km, the excess is 0.3 km — still below both the 20% gate and the 0.8 km gate. Neither distance field carries the claim over the threshold.

The rider's real grievance is the 67-minute runtime against a 44-minute optimal, and that delay is a traffic event, not a route choice. Traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00535-01 is a HIGH-severity multi-vehicle accident on the SLE northbound near the Lentor exit, recorded as intersecting the route and overlapping the trip window by 60 minutes, with a shortest lawful alternative of 22.8 km. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured excess, 1.30 x (22.8 - 20.1) + 1.00) = min(0.25, 4.51) = 0.25 km, so the entire measured excess sits inside the exoneration cap; the closure-adjusted optimal is 20.35 km and zero excess remains. POL-RD-09(2) adds nothing, because the off-route ERP, toll and surcharge lines on this trip are all SGD 0.00.

The rider bears the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from the trace. The claim pleads duration, a missed train and consequential changes; it identifies no distance excess at all, and the artifacts disclose none. An assertion that cites no measurement meeting the threshold carries no weight, and the burden is not discharged.

No repeat-deviation uplift is open to the rider. POL-RD-06 establishes a pattern only where driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3 or more, or where that figure divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 0.05 or more with completed_trips_90d of at least 40. EV-DPROF-00535 records deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 250, a ratio of 0.00, and the clause is in any event consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, which it does not here.

The only money a route-deviation dispute moves on a METERED trip is the arithmetic fare differential computed under POL-RD-02, and only after a deviation is established under POL-RD-01. The fare_breakdown shows the trip charged with no refund issued; the recomputed_fare and refund figures in its derived block are mechanical outputs predicated on a deviation being established and do not themselves establish one. The rider's asserted SGD 200 of train changes is a consequential loss for which the fare model carries no line. With no deviation established, the contested amount stands.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you are entitled to know exactly what decided this. The route-deviation policy prices one thing: distance driven beyond the platform's booked optimal route. On this trip the governing trace (EV-GPS-00535: 100% coverage, 403 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps, weight 1.0) measures 20.35 km against the booked optimal of 20.1 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00535, weight 1.0). That is an excess of 0.25 km, 1.24% of optimal — and under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs over the rounded 20.4 km trip-record copy. POL-RD-01 grants a refund only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km; 0.25 km fails both gates. No deviation is therefore established, and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, save for a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4). Both advocates conceded this threshold, and they are right to have done so.

That disposes of the fare money. The derived refund figures on EV-FARE-00535 (SGD 6.70 against the booked optimal and SGD 6.35 against the closure-adjusted optimal, on a charged total of SGD 38.66 and a recomputed fare of SGD 31.9950 / SGD 32.32250) are mechanical outputs that presuppose an established deviation; they do not establish one. The rider's conditional request for SGD 6.35/6.70 (POL-RD-02) is answered and rejected on that ground: the condition it depends on never arises.

To the rider: your real grievance is the 67-minute runtime against the 44-minute estimate, and the train you missed. That is delay, and this policy does not price delay. On a metered fare the time charge (67 min x SGD 0.28 = SGD 18.76) accrues with the time actually spent in the vehicle, and POL-RD-02's recomputation runs only AFTER a distance deviation is established, which it is not. The SGD 30.00 you contested is the consequential cost of the missed connection, not a line of the metered fare, and the fare model carries no head of loss for it — I accept your own concession to that effect, and I cannot award it. The voucher offer is a commercial matter outside this ruling.

To the driver: you said an accident caused the delay, and the bundle does corroborate you — EV-ADVIS-00535-01 (weight 1.0) is a HIGH-severity LTA DataMall advisory for a multi-vehicle accident on the SLE northbound near the Lentor exit, intersecting the route and overlapping the trip window by 60 minutes. Because no deviation is established there is nothing for POL-RD-03 to exonerate, so I do not need to reach that clause; the measured 0.25 km excess is simply below the POL-RD-01 gates. The clause is likewise not needed for the money: the off-route ERP, toll and surcharge lines on EV-FARE-00535 are all SGD 0.00, so POL-RD-09(2) adds nothing.

No repeat-deviation uplift (POL-RD-06) is in play: EV-DPROF-00535 records deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 250, and POL-RD-06 is consulted only on a material deviation, which this is not. No phantom gantry or airport-surcharge line exists, so POL-RD-09(4) produces no billing-integrity finding and no referral, and no clause-mandated referral fires. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger applies: all three artifacts carry trip_id TRP-00535 with matching pickup timestamps, the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) (no gaps, 10-second cadence), every fare line has a counterpart in the trace or trip record, and the evidence is not contradictory. Same-trip and burden limbs of POL-RD-08 are met on both sides, so nothing turns on the burden's allocation.

Confidence is 0.90. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — sits at weight 1.0, well above the 0.70 floor, so no escalation is warranted and the present state of the charge stands.

Both parties: this is a ROUTE_DEVIATION dispute, and the only thing the policy prices is whether the distance actually driven exceeded the booked optimal route by more than the POL-RD-01 gate. It did not. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure where it disagrees with the rounded trip-record copy. The trace (EV-GPS-00535) records 20.35 km against the booked optimal of 20.1 km — an excess of 0.25 km, 1.24% of optimal. The clause requires the excess to beat both 0.8 km in absolute terms and 20% of optimal; 0.25 km fails both, the platform's own derived status reads 'no deviation', and the rider's own advocate concedes the point. POL-RD-01 therefore directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. On the driver's side, the expressway accident and the LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-00535-01) explain the 67-minute runtime against the 44-minute estimate, but the route-deviation policy does not price delay, and POL-RD-03 exoneration has no deviation to excuse here — the whole measured excess of 0.25 km already sits inside its cap. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00535) is empty: it carries no rider instruction and no driver admission. The rider's asserted consequential losses (the missed connection and SGD 200 of train changes) are not lines of the metered fare — EV-FARE-00535 prices distance, time, base fare and platform fee only, and POL-RD-02 can only move the difference between the charged total of SGD 38.66 and a recomputed optimal-route fare, a computation that is never reached because no deviation is established. The SGD 30.00 contested therefore stands. On the driver profile, no POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern is open (EV-DPROF-00535 records deviation_flags_90d = 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days), so no conduct referral fires, and there is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity line to correct (ERP, tolls and surcharges are all SGD 0.00). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (100% coverage, 403 fixes at 10 s cadence, no gaps) and every artifact relied on sits at weight 1.0, so nothing is discounted and no escalation arises. The charge is left in place: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00 are unchanged.

To both parties. This dispute is a ROUTE_DEVIATION claim over trip TRP-00535, charged SGD 38.66 on a METERED fare (EV-FARE-00535). Under POL-RD-01 no money moves on a route-deviation dispute unless the GPS trace shows a distance excess over the booked optimal route.

The governing measurement is the trace length, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 20.35 km (EV-GPS-00535), read against the booked optimal route of 20.1 km (EV-TRIP-00535). The excess is 0.25 km, which is 1.24% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance (here 4.02 km) AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; both tests must pass, and 0.25 km fails both. The platform's own derived deviation status on the trace reads 'no deviation'. The two advocates agree on this, and so do I. Even on the rounded trip-record figure of 20.4 km, which POL-RD-01 forbids citing for the threshold test, the excess would be 0.3 km and still fail both gates.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's fare recomputation never runs. The recomputed-fare and refund figures sitting in the fare breakdown's derived block (SGD 6.35 against the closure-adjusted optimal, SGD 6.70 against the unadjusted one) are mechanical outputs predicated on a deviation being found; they do not themselves establish one, and neither is payable. The metered charge stands as paid: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, and POL-GEN-03 directs that state be left as it is.

On the rider's points. The rider's difficulty is real but it is a delay, not a route defect: 67 minutes driven against a 44-minute platform estimate. The route-deviation policy prices distance and time only through the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which requires an established deviation first. The SGD 30.00 contested, and the SGD 200 of train changes described, are consequential losses for which the fare model carries no line; POL-RD-02 prices only the distance and time lines of the fare breakdown, and no head of loss is provided for a missed connection. The rider's advocate was candid about this and confined the ask to the conditional SGD 6.35; that condition (an excess sufficient under POL-RD-01) is not met, so the figure is not awarded.

On the driver's points. The driver's assertion of an expressway accident is on file as LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00535-01 (HIGH severity, SLE northbound near Lentor, overlapping the trip window by 60 minutes, weight 1.0). Exoneration under POL-RD-03 presupposes a deviation to excuse; there is none, so the question is moot and changes nothing. The repeat-deviation check under POL-RD-06 is likewise moot — it is consulted only on a MATERIAL deviation — and in any event EV-DPROF-00535 records deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 250, a ratio of 0.00, well short of the clause's 3-flag or 5% tests, so no driver-conduct referral arises. The driver's contention that an uncited or unsupported traffic assertion does not discharge the burden is not reached, because the advisory is present and the case never leaves POL-RD-01.

On evidence quality: all artifacts in the bundle sit at weight_multiplier 1.0 and none is flagged. The GPS trace has 100% coverage, 403 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so it meets none of the impairment limbs (a)-(c) of POL-RD-07 and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: the trip identifiers all read TRP-00535, the timestamps on trip record, trace and ledger are consistent and run forwards, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact, the refund — were one due — is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total, the two sides are not in contradiction, and the fare breakdown carries no ERP, toll or surcharge line at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00), so there is no unmatched charge line and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding. The minute difference between the fare breakdown's two published payable figures (SGD 6.35 and SGD 6.70) is explained by whether the recomputation uses the closure-adjusted or the booked optimal; neither is owed here.

Outcome: no refund to the rider, no compensation to the driver, and the SGD 38.66 charge stands. The deciding fact — that the driven distance did not exceed the booked optimal by the POL-RD-01 threshold — is carried by the trace (EV-GPS-00535) and the trip record (EV-TRIP-00535), both at weight 1.0, so confidence is capped at 1.0; I have set it at 0.95 to allow for ordinary measurement noise. No referral is made: no clause on these facts produces one.

This is a ROUTE_DEVIATION dispute and the policy that governs it measures distance, so the test is distance, not time.

To the rider: the fare of SGD 38.66 on EV-FARE-00535 stands. POL-RD-01 requires the excess of actual over optimal distance to be measured from the GPS trace, because where the trace and the rounded trip-record copy disagree the trace governs and the rounded copy may not be cited for the threshold. EV-GPS-00535 records trace_distance_km = 20.35 km against the booked optimal of 20.1 km (EV-TRIP-00535): an excess of 0.25 km, or 1.24%. Both limbs must pass — the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km — and 0.25 km fails both. No deviation is therefore established, and the platform's own derived deviation status agrees ('no deviation'). POL-RD-02 only ever recomputes the fare after a deviation is established; the SGD 6.35 (or SGD 6.70) figure in the fare breakdown's derived block is a mechanical output predicated on a deviation being found, so I do not award it. Your SGD 30.00 contested sum, the SGD 200 of changes and the missed train are consequential losses the metered fare model carries no line for, and the 67-minute runtime against the 44-minute estimate is a delay rather than a route deviation — the route-deviation policy does not price it. The SGD 100 voucher offers are outside this ruling.

To the driver: your traffic explanation is corroborated — EV-ADVIS-00535-01 is a HIGH-severity SLE northbound accident overlapping the trip window by 60 minutes — but the point does not need deciding, because there is no deviation to exonerate and the measured excess (0.25 km) sits inside the POL-RD-03 exoneration cap (min(0.25, 1.30 x (22.8 - 20.1) + 1.00) = 0.25 km) in any event. No billing-integrity defect arises under POL-RD-09(4): every ERP, toll and airport-surcharge line on EV-FARE-00535 is SGD 0.00, and no gantry is charged that the trace does not cross.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The charge is left as recorded, no refund issues to the rider and no compensation is due to the driver. Confidence 0.90, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts (EV-GPS-00535 and EV-TRIP-00535) that carry the deciding fact. No referral and no escalation: the trip identifiers match across all three instruments, the trace is complete (100% coverage, 403 fixes, 10-second cadence, no gaps), and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires — in particular the traffic advisory the driver relies on is present in the bundle, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged.
